::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Dec 6th [1866]  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection, CO171: Box 29
:::

My dear [Anne](people/person_930.qmd)
[Mrs Keble](people/person_797.qmd) has just returned me this, it had no end to it and I hope it ought not. How very interesting it is and how heart stirring [Miss Arthur](people/person_65.qmd)’s letter, which I am sending to Mrs T Keble.[^1] Our [Nets](organizations/other_94.qmd) are not come yet. I forgot to tell you of Miss Parkes’ [Vignettes](other_books/otherbook_476.qmd) to order. I think you would find much to interest you

Your most affectionate
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The enclosure was no doubt some comment on the recent death of [John Keble](people/person_798.qmd) and his wife, about which CMY had been corresponding with his sister-in-law Elizabeth Jane Keble (Mrs Thomas Keble).  Anne Mackenzie edited a missionary magazine called *The Net*, and Mary Arthur, a missionary in South Africa, was probably one of her correspondents.
